what_its_for: Fondaparinux is a blood thinner (anticoagulant) used to prevent or treat dangerous blood clots. It is commonly used to prevent blood clots in your legs (deep vein thrombosis, or DVT) or lungs (pulmonary embolism, or PE), especially after hip or knee replacement surgery, hip fracture surgery, or abdominal surgery. It can also be used to treat blood clots that have already formed.
how_to_take: Fondaparinux is given as an injection under the skin (subcutaneous injection), usually in the fatty area of your stomach (abdomen). Your doctor, nurse, or pharmacist will teach you how to give yourself this shot at home. Always inject in a different spot each time to avoid skin irritation. Do not inject into muscle. Use each prefilled syringe only once and throw it away safely in a sharps container after use. Inject at the same time each day.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose based on your weight and the reason you are taking this medication. The usual dose for prevention of blood clots is 2.5 mg once daily. For treatment of blood clots, the dose is based on your body weight (typically 5 mg, 7.5 mg, or 10 mg once daily). Always follow your doctor's instructions exactly. Do not change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, inject it as soon as you remember on the same day. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not inject two doses on the same day or double up to make up for a missed dose. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store fondaparinux at room temperature between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep it away from light, heat, and moisture. Do not freeze. Keep it out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of used syringes in an approved sharps container — never throw them in regular trash. Ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of your sharps container.
what_to_avoid: Avoid activities that increase your risk of bleeding or injury, such as contact sports or other rough activities. Avoid taking aspirin, ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin), naproxen (Aleve), or other anti-inflammatory pain relievers unless your doctor approves, as these can increase your risk of bleeding. Tell your dentist or any other healthcare provider that you are taking this medication before any procedure or surgery. Avoid alcohol in large amounts, as it can also increase bleeding risk.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you notice: unusual bruising or bleeding that won't stop, blood in your urine (pink or red color) or stools (red or black tarry stools), coughing or vomiting blood, severe headache, dizziness, or weakness, numbness or tingling especially in your legs or feet (this could be a sign of a serious spinal problem if you had a spinal procedure), swelling or severe pain at the injection site, signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face, lips, or throat, or difficulty breathing.
when_it_works: Fondaparinux starts working within a few hours of your first injection. However, you may not feel any different because it works quietly in your bloodstream to prevent clots from forming or getting bigger. It is important to take it every day as prescribed, even if you feel well. Your doctor will monitor your blood work periodically to make sure the medication is working safely.
special_populations: Kidney problems: This medication is removed from your body by your kidneys. If you have kidney disease, your doctor will monitor you closely and may adjust your dose or choose a different medication. Fondaparinux should not be used if you have severe kidney problems. Elderly patients: Older adults may be more sensitive to this medication and have a higher risk of bleeding. Extra caution and monitoring are needed. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Fondaparinux should only be used during pregnancy if clearly needed. It is unknown if it passes into breast milk. Children: This medication is generally not recommended for children under 17 years of age.
